title: Read-only local Windows PowerShell environment A/B

method.stderrPolicy: Persist only fixed recognized diagnostic markers and byte/line counts; omit raw stderr text.
method.additionalVariableProbeReason: Neither primary case failed; no failure to isolate.

findings: Both exact filtered queries succeeded within 0.406 seconds; no timeout, nonzero exit or stderr was observed.
The eight-key environment, lacking windir/USERPROFILE/PSModulePath, returned one valid WinWS result with the same stdout size as inherited environment.
This local result does not establish the cause of the actual hosted LocalSystem component.query failures.
No production whitelist/environment fix is supported by this A/B result.

securityDecision.conditionalFutureChange: Only after an actual SYSTEM failure is isolated to one missing variable, derive that value from a trusted system path/current service account API and add only that key; do not copy the caller environment.
securityDecision.psModulePathTradeoff: An inherited/user-writable module search path would allow untrusted module resolution in a privileged worker; a demonstrated requirement would need fixed machine-owned PSHOME modules only.

minimalDecisiveHostedDiagnostic: At the original worker execFile boundary capture safe code/killed/signal/elapsed/stdoutBytes/stderrBytes and sanitized fixed error markers before JS wraps error.message.
Run only the same Name=winws.exe read-only query under the actual sealed LocalSystem worker host; do not persist process fields or change SCM/network state.
If the same eight-key environment then fails, separate child startup/module import/CIM provider phases with safe markers before any environment, timeout or ownership change.
limitations: Actual current user token administrativeToken=false/systemToken=false; no SYSTEM or elevated child was started.
Physical Windows10.0.26200.0 differs from the hosted failing Windows10.0.26100.0 runner.
Probe parent is external Node24.19.0, not the installed fused Electron worker; its cwd/TEMP are isolated own-work paths rather than actual installation/private service paths.
Normal case inherits the actual PS7.6.5-host PSModulePath, including PS7 and WinPS modules; it is not a claimed Explorer or SYSTEM environment.
Only two sequential children were executed. This is a bounded reproduction check, not a latency benchmark, concurrency/load test or uptime guarantee.
No repeat, one-variable repair probes, Setup, application/service launch, SCM/DNS/Tasks/registry mutation, unrelated process kill, GUI operation or external API mutation was performed.

primaryReferences.claim: execFile env/timeout/error fields and direct executable behavior.
Windows PowerShell startup builds module search defaults when PSModulePath is absent; PS7/WinPS module-path handling differs.
Local Get-CimInstance without ComputerName or CimSession uses local WMI/COM.
